name: Altscherbitz timber frame with wedged tenons
description: The Altscherbitz Neolithic well lining has a basal timber frame with wedged mortise-and-tenon joints and interlocking corners.

impact.note: One well lining in one early farming village, an early witness to sound timber joints that improved a well; no descent from it is known.

date.label: 5102 BCE timber felling to 5099 BCE construction-pit plank
date.basis: This dates the scoped witness or event, not a claim of global invention.

events.statement: The Altscherbitz Neolithic well lining has a basal timber frame with wedged mortise-and-tenon joints and interlocking corners.

evidence.locator: Results, well A; figures 4–5 and S1
evidence.supports: Well A at Altscherbitz has a mortise-and-tenon basal frame with projecting tenons secured by wooden wedges; its oak construction timbers derive from 13 trees felled in 5102 BCE, and a pit plank is dated to 5099 BCE.

events.caveats: The 5102 BCE date applies to the identified oak felling and 5099 BCE to a plank from the construction pit, which authors treat as evidence for construction onset. They are not a direct measurement of every construction step or an origin claim.

links.statement: The Altscherbitz builders used split oak timbers for the well lining, whose basal frame includes wedged mortise-and-tenon joints.
links.scope: Timber preparation for the Altscherbitz well assembly.
links.caveats: The beam preparation is documented at Altscherbitz. The planks at Ostrov show the process in use elsewhere. Movement of workers or know-how between the projects remains unresolved.

evidence.locator: Results, Well A, figs. 3–4, S8 and S9
evidence.supports: The researchers reconstructed splitting from the timbers and tree-ring series. They identify oak beams split radially and tangentially from the trees used in Well A.

evidence.locator: §3.1 Trace evidence, table 1, figs. 6–8; §3.2 Dendrochronology and radiocarbon dating
evidence.supports: The Ostrov study reports a separately excavated application, mainly radially split oak planks with one tangentially split plank.
The documented Altscherbitz frame forms the base of the well lining and uses wedged tenon joints.
